claims.claim: Beim Auerhuhn kommen zur Laufbefiederung in der kalten Jahresphase seitliche hornige Zehenstifte hinzu. Die auch Balzstifte genannten Strukturen vergrößern die Auftrittsfläche und vermindern das Einsinken auf weichem Schnee; keine Monats- oder vollständige Einsinkgarantie wird behauptet.

sourceProcedure: The four named institutions publish their own original educational species accounts. BirdLife, NABU and Naturpark Bayerischer Wald independently describe capercaillie pectinations and snow support; BirdLife and the Swiss National Park separately support the Alpine ptarmigan toe-feather comparison. These are institutional expert accounts, not experiments, measurements or claimed independent experimental replications. Root confirmed separate direct reading of all four pages before implementation.
boundaries: Only Tetrao urogallus and the explicit Lagopus muta comparison; no universal uniform Raufusshuhn foot.
Different structures, no claim that feather and horn pectination have chemically different materials or a stated developmental/evolutionary origin.
No fixed months, measurements, loading calculations, sex/age diagnosis or photos used as a species guarantee.
No guarantee against any sinking or cold injury; no field disturbance exercise, legal or hunting-release claim.
Own simplified paper comparison is explicit; no unprovided illustration is promised.
Complete explanation and visible limits precede the collapsed final source appendix.
notUsed: Search-discovered historical or glossary wording describing pectinations as modified feathers was not adopted; the bounded text makes no origin claim.

media.reason: No new photograph, diagram or third-party visual was needed. Own paper exercise is clearly a learner activity.
